hunks.baseline: Humans are animals that learn.
hunks.sol: Humans are creatures that learn.

hunks.baseline: Of course, they often forget important things. But if they forgot everything without ever learning a thing, humanity as we know it wouldn’t exist.
hunks.sol: Of course, they sometimes forget important things. But if they forgot everything without ever learning a thing, humanity as we know it wouldn’t exist.

hunks.baseline: And over millions of years, they developed without end.
hunks.sol: Over millions of years, they never stopped advancing.

hunks.baseline: They learned to use fire and chip away at stone, until at last they glimpsed the boundless world of empty space above the clouds.
hunks.sol: They learned to use fire and shape stone, until at last they glimpsed the boundless void above the clouds.

hunks.baseline: But for humanity, which had built a great civilization over such an unfathomable stretch of time, the past thirty-odd years were far too short to forget the horrific catastrophe named the Great Cataclysm.
hunks.sol: But for humanity, which had built a great civilization over such an unfathomable stretch of time, thirty-odd years were far too short to forget the horrific catastrophe known as the Great Cataclysm.

hunks.baseline: Faster than magical power rising from the frozen lands of the Far East could stain the sky, and with an urgency that couldn’t even be compared to it.
hunks.sol: It spread faster than the magical power rising from the frozen lands of the Far East could stain the sky, with an urgency beyond comparison.

hunks.baseline: Naturally, every available person and resource was thrown into action without restraint.
hunks.sol: Every available person and resource was mobilized.

hunks.baseline: Governments declared martial law and deployed the military to evacuate their citizens to safe zones. The whole process moved swiftly and efficiently.
hunks.sol: Governments declared martial law and deployed their militaries to evacuate citizens to safe zones. The process was swift and orderly.

hunks.baseline: For better or worse, ever since Morgoth appeared, people had been gripped by fear. They’d already evacuated, or made all the preparations to do so at a moment’s notice.
hunks.sol: For better or worse, the fear that had gripped people since Morgoth’s appearance meant they had either evacuated already or were ready to leave at a moment’s notice.

hunks.baseline: But even those still beneath the blue sky faced no less danger.
hunks.sol: But those still beneath the blue sky faced no less danger.

hunks.baseline: As magical power spiraled out of control, countless Gates scattered around the world began opening their dark maws, one after another. Monsters poured out of that cursed world, rampaging with greater strength and savagery.
hunks.sol: As magical power spiraled out of control, countless Gates scattered around the world opened their dark maws, one after another. Monsters poured out of that cursed world, rampaging with greater strength and savagery.

hunks.baseline: The ground trembled at the vibrations coming from far away.
hunks.sol: The ground trembled at vibrations coming from far away.

hunks.baseline: The middle-aged man grinned, showing his teeth between bristly whiskers. The young man might have been annoyed for a moment, but instead he swallowed hard and answered.
hunks.sol: The middle-aged man grinned, showing his teeth through his bristly beard. The young man might have been annoyed, but he swallowed hard and answered.

hunks.baseline: “Sure you are. It’s obvious. Just be honest.”
hunks.sol: “Sure you are. I can tell. Just be honest.”

hunks.baseline: “Well, the truth is, a little.”
hunks.sol: “Well… a little.”

hunks.baseline: “Look at this guy. You call yourself a Hunter, and you’re already scared before the fight’s even started?”
hunks.sol: “Look at this guy. You call yourself a Hunter, and you’re scared before the fight’s even started?”

hunks.baseline: The young man’s face fell in an instant. The middle-aged man, who’d been putting on a stern expression, and the Hunters around them all chuckled.
hunks.sol: The young man’s face fell. The middle-aged man, who’d only been pretending to look stern, chuckled, and so did the Hunters around them.

hunks.baseline: “Now, now. A grown man shouldn’t cry over something like this. We’ve all been through it once. Back in my day…”
hunks.sol: “Come on. What kind of man cries over this? We’ve all been through it. Back in my day…”

hunks.baseline: [^1]: The Korean phrase for “back in my day” sounds like “latte,” setting up the instant-coffee joke.
In this serious situation, where he should have been on edge, what was this conversation that made him lose all his nerve just listening to it?
hunks.sol: This was a serious situation. He ought to be on edge. So why was their conversation enough to drain every bit of tension out of him?

hunks.baseline: The young man hadn’t had a choice in the first place.
hunks.sol: He hadn’t had a choice in the first place.

hunks.baseline: And the person who’d “picked up” this twenty-year-old and brought him into a veteran party with an average age of 41.5 suddenly spoke.
hunks.sol: The man who’d “picked up” this twenty-year-old and brought him into a veteran party with an average age of 41.5 spoke up.

hunks.baseline: The young man blinked for a moment, then answered.
His voice was much calmer than before, but even more bewildered.
hunks.sol: The young man blinked, then answered in a voice much calmer than before, though even more bewildered.

hunks.baseline: “Good. But I understand either way. It’s natural to shake at first. Your nerves are bound to be on edge.”
hunks.sol: “Well, I’d understand if you did. Everyone’s nervous at first. You can’t help being on edge.”

hunks.baseline: The middle-aged man patted the young man’s shoulder encouragingly and laughed out loud.
hunks.sol: The middle-aged man gave his shoulder an encouraging pat and laughed.

hunks.baseline: It was a friendly laugh, hard to believe coming from a face that could make even the most vicious criminal think twice.
hunks.sol: It was such a warm laugh that it was hard to believe it came from a man whose face could make even a hardened criminal back down.

hunks.baseline: Maybe that was why the young man, who was at the bottom of the pecking order in this veteran party, decided to work up the courage to speak.
hunks.sol: Maybe that was why the young man, who hardly dared open his mouth in this veteran party, worked up the courage to speak.

hunks.baseline: When the middle-aged man readily nodded, the young man cautiously continued.
hunks.sol: The middle-aged man readily nodded, and the young man cautiously continued.

hunks.baseline: “Why did you choose me…”
hunks.sol: “Why did you choose me…?”

hunks.baseline: But that was enough for the middle-aged man to understand. He answered without a moment’s hesitation.
hunks.sol: But that was enough. The middle-aged man answered without a moment’s hesitation.

hunks.baseline: “Yeah. You were working really hard. Hard enough to look desperate.”
hunks.sol: “Yeah. You were working hard. Hard enough to look desperate.”

hunks.baseline: That was right.
hunks.sol: That was true.

hunks.baseline: Two days ago, when the two of them first met, hundreds of rookies who’d just graduated from the regional Hunter training center had gathered there, showing off as they waited for their team assignments.
hunks.sol: Two days ago, when they’d first met, hundreds of rookies fresh out of the regional Hunter training center had gathered there, showing what they could do while they waited for their team assignments.

hunks.baseline: They wanted to get into a team with a better chance of survival.
hunks.sol: They wanted a team with a better chance of survival.

hunks.baseline: Not to earn more money like before, but to protect the one thing they couldn’t trade for anything: their lives.
hunks.sol: Not to earn more money, as they once might have, but to protect the one thing they couldn’t trade for anything: their lives.

hunks.baseline: And of all those rookies, the young man had been the only one who wasn’t there.
hunks.sol: And of all those rookies, the young man had been the only one who’d left the room.

hunks.baseline: “Outside. I needed to find somewhere without people, somewhere with a little space.”
hunks.sol: “Outside. I needed to find somewhere without people, somewhere with a bit of space.”

hunks.baseline: “You could’ve done it there, like everyone else, and used it to show off, couldn’t you? Everyone knows the people in charge watch the waiting room through the monitor room.”
hunks.sol: “You could’ve trained in there like everyone else and shown them what you could do, couldn’t you? Even ordinary people know the staff watch the waiting room from the monitor room.”

hunks.baseline: Naturally. It was a waiting room, not a training room for the official test. It was fairly spacious, but with so many people swinging around bladed weapons, it would have been hard to concentrate.
hunks.sol: Of course he couldn’t. It was a waiting room, not the training room used for official tests. Spacious as it was, anyone would have trouble concentrating with that many people swinging bladed weapons around.

hunks.baseline: The act of training might have been the same, but his reason for doing it was entirely different.
hunks.sol: He might have been doing the same thing as the others, but his reason for doing it was entirely different.

hunks.baseline: He was working with all his heart.
hunks.sol: He was giving the training everything he had.

hunks.baseline: That day, after secretly following the young man, the middle-aged man had watched him train alone in an empty lot. The sight brought back a memory from a few years ago.
hunks.sol: That day, the middle-aged man had secretly followed him to an empty lot. Watching him train there alone brought back a memory from a few years ago.

hunks.baseline: “The friend I mentioned earlier. I ran into him at a Hunter manpower office. He was young, like you—no, younger. A rookie at a glance. I figured I wouldn’t be seeing him for long.”
hunks.sol: “The friend I mentioned earlier. I met him at a Hunter manpower office. He was young, like you—no, he was just a kid. A rookie at a glance. I figured I wouldn’t be seeing him for long.”

hunks.baseline: At the word, the young man understood.
hunks.sol: That one word was enough for the young man to understand.

hunks.baseline: The young man had even thought the same thing on the day he got his first rank assessment, when he saw the E on the monitor:
hunks.sol: Even the young man, on the day of his first rank assessment, had looked at the E glowing on the monitor and thought:

hunks.baseline: “At first, I didn’t know I’d keep seeing him for over half a year.”
hunks.sol: “At first, I had no idea I’d keep seeing him for over half a year.”

hunks.baseline: Most people would’ve quit by then.
hunks.sol: Most people would have quit by then.

hunks.baseline: That is, if they’d been ordinary people.
hunks.sol: If they were ordinary people, that is.

hunks.baseline: “He wasn’t. He’d leave a perfectly good sofa behind and climb the hill behind the office, training like hell every day. Like some guy I saw two days ago.”
hunks.sol: “He didn’t. He’d leave a perfectly good sofa behind, climb the hill behind the office, and train like hell every day. Like some guy I saw two days ago.”

hunks.baseline: “He’d take a number, train, come back when his turn was up, get turned down like always, take another number, train again… He never even got near a Gate, but by closing time at the office he’d be more exhausted than someone who’d done five runs in a day.”
hunks.sol: “He’d take a number, train, come back when his turn was up, get turned down like always, take another number, train again… He never even got near a Gate, but by closing time he’d be more exhausted than someone who’d done five runs in a day.”

hunks.baseline: “Right? And here’s the funny part: his face always looked miserable, and his mouth was going *fuck, fuck, fuck*, but he trained harder than anyone I’d ever seen. He wasn’t doing it because it was easy. He did it even though it was hard. Every single day.”
hunks.sol: “Right? And here’s the funny part: he always looked miserable and kept mouthing *fuck, fuck*, but he trained harder than anyone I’d ever seen. He didn’t do it because he found it easy. He did it even though it was hard. Every single day.”

hunks.baseline: “Yeah. He was an incredible guy.”
hunks.sol: “Yeah. He’s an incredible guy.”

hunks.baseline: “If you saw him every day for half a year, doesn’t that mean you were doing the same thing he was?”
hunks.sol: “If you saw him every day for half a year, doesn’t that mean you were doing the same thing?”

hunks.baseline: It wasn’t just flattery.
hunks.sol: It wasn’t flattery.

hunks.baseline: Just as the middle-aged man had watched the young man, the young man had been watching his superior closely, too.
hunks.sol: Just as the middle-aged man had watched him, the young man had been watching his superior closely, too.

hunks.baseline: He’d only known him for two days, so it was a stretch to say he’d watched him for long. But he’d seen more than enough to know he was someone worth respecting.
hunks.sol: Two days was hardly any time at all, but it had been more than enough to see that the man deserved his respect.

hunks.baseline: “Yes. You have character, skill, and you work hard. I even saw a news article about you once. I remember the headline: *From F-rank to B-rank: A Hunter’s Life of Extraordinary Ups and Downs.*”
hunks.sol: “Yes. You have character, skill, and you work hard. I even saw a news article about you once. I remember the headline: *From F-rank to B-rank: One Hunter’s Extraordinary Ups and Downs.*”

hunks.baseline: The young man had dredged up an embarrassing chapter of his life that the middle-aged man would rather forget. Laughter broke out around them, and the middle-aged man scratched his bushy beard, his face turning red.
hunks.sol: The young man had dredged up an embarrassing chapter of his life that the middle-aged man would rather forget. Laughter broke out around them, and he scratched his bushy beard, his face turning red.

hunks.baseline: Just as he started to stammer out a reply, his expression suddenly hardened.
hunks.sol: He was just about to stammer out a reply when his expression hardened.

hunks.baseline: The vibrations were stronger than they’d been ten minutes ago. Now they weren’t just coming up through the soles of their feet; they were shaking their whole bodies.
hunks.sol: The vibrations were stronger than they’d been ten minutes ago. Now he felt them not just through the soles of his feet, but through his entire body.

hunks.baseline: Everyone felt it at once, and realized anew how close they were to death.
hunks.sol: Everyone felt it at once, and realized anew how close they stood to death.

hunks.baseline: “Thanks for saying I’m someone’s dream.”
hunks.sol: “For saying I’m someone’s dream. Thanks.”

hunks.baseline: Even now, the middle-aged man—Im Kkeokjeong, Team Leader of Ares Guild’s Team 32—hadn’t lost his smile. He pulled his helmet down low and thought:
hunks.sol: Still smiling, the middle-aged man—Im Kkeokjeong, Team Leader of Ares Guild’s Team 32—pulled his helmet down low.

hunks.baseline: Then he fixed his gaze on the dust cloud rising a few hundred meters away and shouted with all his might:
hunks.sol: He fixed his gaze on the dust cloud rising a few hundred meters away and shouted with all his might.

hunks.baseline: —All Hunters, listen. Alpha—Alpha has awakened.
hunks.sol: —Attention, all Hunters. Alpha—Alpha has awakened.
